ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the OSFI Consolidated List, United Nations Security Council sanctions regulations, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act regulations, FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) guidance, and the OFAC SDN List where U.S. dollar payments are anticipated. statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, the corporate name must be in French or have a French form; transliteration into the Latin alphabet is required; names in another language must be accompanied by a French version or approved by the Registraire, with strict application of Quebec naming standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a refusal of a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, including a corrected or alternative name; if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Québec (Tribunal administratif du Québec) within 60 days of the denial; final judicial review before the Superior Court of Québec may be sought with leave. Name reservations may be renewed for an additional 90 days before expiry, subject to the same search and screening procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute for the registered office; the registered office must be a physical address in Quebec where legal process can be served. A virtual administrative or correspondence address may be used for business mail, but it cannot satisfy the statutory registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 5% annual baseline probability for a non-licensed digital advertising services corporation, increasing to elevated risk if FINTRAC or regulatory bodies detect unusual wire transfers, UBO concealment indicators, or inconsistent commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 3, 9, 13, 15-16, 18-19, 71; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 25-29, 31, 35-36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), Office of the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation / Statuts de constitution, followed by the enterprise registration filing with REQ
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec business corporation; shares may be issued for adequate consideration in money, property, or past service. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription of the named subscriber for 100 common shares, and the shares are issued as fully paid upon receipt of the agreed contribution, which constitutes adequate consideration.
RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [registered office address], Quebec, and the secretary is directed to file the declaration of registered office with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President, [name] is appointed Secretary, and [name] is appointed Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until a successor is appointed, with authority to execute all documents and open banking accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search and availability clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online name search / NUANS system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the REQ enterprise register to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinguishing and not confusing with existing registrants. If a word name is used, obtain a NUANS report or REQ preclearance reference. If a numbered company is preferred, request a legal number from REQ and omit the name from the articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or request for a numbered company
NUANS name search report or REQ preclearance reference
Name and address of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file amended articles or resubmit a new application with a revised name, supporting consent letters, and distinguishability arguments within the REQ response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of incorporation dossiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary and REQ prescribed forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation on the REQ prescribed form, setting out share classes, share rights, restrictions, first directors, and the initial registered office in Quebec. The incorporator must sign the articles; standard filings are made digitally and do not require notarization unless REQ requests a certified copy. Prepare each director's signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ articles of incorporation form
Signed consent of each director to act
Initial registered office address in Quebec
NUANS name search report or REQ name preclearance
Incorporator and director identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ identifies a technical defect, make a corrective filing or resubmit the affected page within 30 days. For a material omission after incorporation, file articles of amendment rather than restarting the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online submission and payment with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online service, select the constitution of a legal person transaction, upload the executed articles and director consents, and pay the applicable filing fee by credit card or Interac. Upon approval, REQ issues the attestation of constitution and automatically registers the enterprise in the Quebec enterprise register.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of incorporation
Director consent forms
Registered office address declaration
Payment of the official filing fee
Incorporator and director identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the submission is queried, review the REQ notice, correct the error, and refile promptly. If the document has already been published, file an application for rectification with REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate governance and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary; REQ for declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent, adopt by-laws, issue share certificates to the subscriber, appoint officers, and approve the opening of corporate bank accounts. Maintain the securities register, directors register, and minute book in Quebec. Ensure REQ has received the declaration of registered office and list of directors.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
Adopted by-laws
Share certificates and securities register
Minutes of organizational meeting
REQ declaration of registered office and directors
Registered office lease or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate records are challenged by lenders or authorities, ratify the missing act by a unanimous board resolution and file a corrective declaration with REQ within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, payroll, and banking account registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec, Canada Revenue Agency, CNESST, and financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the attestation of constitution is received, register the corporation for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and Quebec QST through the relevant CRA/Revenu Quebec business registration process. If employees will be hired, register the employer with CNESST for workplace accident insurance. Open a corporate bank account using the attestation, REQ extract, and the banking resolution from the first board meeting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution / REQ attestation
Up-to-date REQ enterprise extract
Board resolution for account opening and authorized signatories
Identification of directors and officers
CRA and Revenu Quebec registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is pending, operate using the temporary business number and provide the attestation as proof of formation. Correct any registration inconsistencies using the CRA and Revenu Quebec online modification services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial or manufacturing regulator is engaged for digital advertising media buying and affiliate lead generation under NAICS 541810.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required for this administrative commercial activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required; pure office-based administrative activity does not trigger a prescribed EIA category under the Quebec Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge is generated by the described affiliate media-buying operations. The corporation must comply with the host building's occupational health and local municipal environmental nuisance bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety or structural license is triggered for an office-based media-buying business. The leased premises must have a valid building occupancy certificate and comply with the Quebec Fire Safety Code. If employees are present in Quebec, the corporation must register with the CNESST for workplace accident and occupational health coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal tax authority and Business Registration Online (BRO) portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; co-administration with Revenu Quebec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca) for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec corporate income tax and provincial payroll obligations under the Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement. The CRA Business Number (BN) is the master federal tax identifier; the QST account (BN suffix 'RM') is the Quebec value-added tax identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Quebec must (1) obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; (2) apply for a CRA Business Number (BN) with the RC (Part I corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST) and RP (payroll) program accounts through BRO or Form RC1 (online issuance is immediate); (3) register for QST with Revenu Quebec (same BN with 'RM' program code; online via 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' or Form LM-1-V) before commencing taxable supplies in Quebec; and (4) if the corporation is a non-resident registrant, appoint a representative for service in Canada under Excise Tax Act section 299. GST/HST and QST registration becomes mandatory immediately once worldwide taxable supplies exceed the $30,000 CAD small-supplier threshold; below the threshold voluntary registration is recommended to recover input tax credits (ITCs) on media inventory, SaaS tools and agency operating costs. CRA and Revenu Quebec exchange registration data automatically, so a single BN application satisfies both authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Canadian Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate legal taxpayer: Part I federal corporate income tax plus Quebec Part I corporate tax are assessed on the corporation itself (Income Tax Act, section 15; Quebec Taxation Act), with no pass-through of income to shareholders. Dividend distributions trigger shareholder-level taxation with integration relief (dividend tax credit / refundable dividend tax on hand). Provincial allocation follows the permanent establishment formula via the T2 return; residency is governed by central management and control; non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax, potentially treaty-reduced.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime; legal-form corporations are automatically taxed at the entity level. Available statutory elections include: (a) the GST/HST joint election for closely related corporations (Excise Tax Act, section 156) and its mirror QST election, which deems qualifying intercompany supplies to be made for nil consideration; (b) the capital dividend account election (Form T2054, ITA section 83(2)); (c) the section 216 election replacing Part XIII withholding with a net Canadian return for certain rental and royalty-type income; (d) associated-corporation elections and waivers governing the small business deduction (ITA sections 125 and 256); and (e) hybrid-arrangement limitation rules in ITA sections 18.4 to 18.6 (BEPS Action 2), which disallow double-deduction and deduction-without-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax at 5%) combined with QST (Quebec Sales Tax at 9.975%) - a coordinated dual-VAT regime administered jointly by CRA and Revenu Quebec under the Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement. Supplies made in Quebec carry a combined headline rate of 14.975%; imported media-buying and advertising services acquired by the Canadian corporation are generally subject to the reverse-charge / self-assessment rules where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD of annual worldwide taxable supplies, net of capital-property sales (the GST/HST and QST 'small supplier' threshold). Registration is mandatory immediately upon exceeding the threshold; a foreign supplier making taxable supplies in Canada in the ordinary course must register, and a non-resident may register voluntarily to claim ITCs. Quebec applies the same $30,000 threshold for QST; there is no separate provincial monetary threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting gateway, or continuous-transaction-control digital stamping regime exists at the CRA or Revenu Quebec level; Canada operates a self-assessment VAT model with ex-post audit. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding $1.5M CAD, and all QST returns are filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's secure business portal. Invoices may be issued in any medium provided they contain the BN, supply date, description, consideration and the applicable GST/HST/QST amount or a zero-rating indicator. E-invoicing interoperability is voluntary (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 is the emerging public-sector standard); records must be maintained in an electronically retrievable format under section 286 of the Excise Tax Act and section 230 of the Income Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported services applies under Excise Tax Act section 23 and mirror QST provisions: a supply of digital advertising, media-buying arbitrage and affiliate lead-generation services is 0%-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not registered for GST/HST or QST at the time of supply, unless the service relates to (i) real property situated in Canada, (ii) tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance, or (iii) an individual who benefits from the service while physically present in Canada. Services directed to foreign markets (foreign-media advertising, offshore affiliate traffic, foreign campaign management) are additionally covered by the advertising-services export rule in ETA section 23.1 where distribution occurs through non-Canadian media. For QST, the supply likewise falls outside Quebec tax when the recipient's business is foreign and the service is not consumed in Quebec. The supplier must obtain written non-resident evidence (residency certificates, foreign VAT registration numbers, address and OFAC verification) and an executed export-service contract to substantiate the 0% claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Form B13A proves physical exit for any tangible media or promotional collateral bundled with the service; pure digital service exports are substantiated by a service-export evidence dossier (contract, invoices, campaign delivery logs and technical performance data)

Bill of Lading - required where physical materials or promotional goods are shipped internationally; for digital-only deliverables, substitute the carriage contract, delivery receipts and server/access logs

Inward Remittance Certificate - bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103, or Mercury-ACH/Wise transaction record evidencing receipt of foreign-currency consideration from the non-resident client within the repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims for exported services attract joint CRA/Revenu Quebec audit scrutiny under export-substantiation programs. If non-resident status or the offshore-consumption test fails, the supply is recharacterized as taxable in Canada and the registrant must remit the uncollected GST/HST/QST (14.975% in Quebec) plus: (a) daily compound interest (statutory base rate plus 2% federally; equivalent provincial daily rate for QST); (b) a 10% negligence penalty on unremitted tax under ETA section 280 and a 10% penalty on overclaimed rebates or refunds under ETA section 285; and (c) criminal prosecution for tax evasion under ITA section 239 and ETA section 326, with fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for repeated or reckless misconduct. Reassessment windows extend from the normal four-year limitation period to ten years (and indefinitely for fraud or wilful misrepresentation), permitting full retrospective clawback of zero-rated turnovers and any input tax credits previously recovered on the underlying media inventory and operating costs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acting with the Department of Finance Canada; prudential bank regulation is delegated to OSFI, and FINTRAC supervises AML/CFT obligations for banks and money-services businesses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully liberalized capital and current account regime under a floating Canadian dollar. There is no Foreign Exchange Control Act constraining capital inflows, profit remittance, or dividend distributions; non-resident taxation is addressed through Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding rather than exchange-control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-receipt surrender or mandatory CAD conversion timeline exists. Export proceeds may be retained in any permitted currency; only general reporting obligations apply, including FINTRAC electronic funds-transfer reports above CAD 10,000 and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments survey filings.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High. Canadian-regulated digital payment institutions and foreign EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Montreal-based Nuvei are viable as settlement rails when registered as money-services businesses with FINTRAC. They cannot provide deposit insurance or full chartered-bank services, so core liquidity must remain with a Schedule I bank while EMIs optimize cross-border conversion and low-value affiliate payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: OSFI and Quebec law do not mandate physical board attendance. Most Schedule I banks accept remote video-KYC onboarding for Canadian-resident directors; however, a non-resident or U.S.-person director combined with a Medium-Risk_Enhanced industry profile normally triggers a notarized corporate resolution, certified director identification, Quebec registered-office endorsement, and either an in-branch interview at a Montreal business centre or a live video interview with the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity and cross-border affiliate-payout patterns typical of performance media buying.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements; executed Master Services Agreements with advertisers and affiliate networks; platform billing statements from Google Ads, Meta, and TikTok; a rolling 12-month cash-flow projection; and a counterparty whitelist with supporting due-diligence files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership or opaque multi-level shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, register of directors with certified passports, source-of-wealth declaration, apostilled notarized resolutions, and an updated ownership transparency chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: In-and-out flows lacking economic substance or mismatched payment narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file comprising office lease, employee payroll records, advertiser settlement statements, invoicing trail, and payment-processor reconciliation reports demonstrating verifiable commercial margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk jurisdiction exposure through foreign media markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML and sanctions-screening policy, geo-blocking evidence, OFSI and UN sanctioned-list screening reports for all downstream payees, and independent due-diligence reports on each foreign affiliate counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must arrive via SWIFT MT103 to a Schedule I bank with field-70 purpose-of-payment text reading 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / DIRECT INVESTMENT', accompanied by a board resolution, share-subscription agreement, and Statistics Canada direct-investment survey identifier. FINTRAC EFT reporting applies above CAD 10,000; Investment Canada Act notification is required only if the controlling non-Canadian investor exceeds statutory review thresholds, which is not anticipated at the projected capital levels.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Large publisher and media-supplier payments settle via SWIFT MT103 priority wires; SWIFT MT700 commercial letters of credit are reserved for physical-goods arbitrage transactions; low-value recurring disbursements clear through Payments Canada ACSS and cross-border ACH; affiliate referrals and sub-affiliate payouts use Wise, Payoneer, or Nuvei. All outbound transfers above CAD 10,000 require FINTRAC reporting and a purpose code classified as 'Digital Advertising Services'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX outright forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, capped at 12-month tenors
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted currencies such as offshore CNY, INR, and KRW, executed only through the bank's licensed dealing desk and supported by documented media-buying exposure
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD funding and treasury alignment, permissible under Canadian derivative regulations when used for end-user hedging
FX vanilla options and zero-cost collars, limited to hedges of demonstrable exposure and capped at 110% of forecast foreign-currency spend to prevent speculative overlay

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration with the REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 66 late fee per year; prolonged non-filing triggers REQ inspection, temporary suspension of legal personality, and administrative dissolution or cancellation of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - only if the corporation is federally incorporated or continued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of federal incorporation or continuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 late fee; overdue return after one year triggers notice of default; after three consecutive years of default, the corporation is dissolved and struck off the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Federal Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; any balance of tax due 3 months after year-end (CCPC) or 2 months after year-end (non-CCPC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated non-compliance triggers 10% plus 2% per month; gross negligence penalty up to 50%.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for distributing or public corporations, or where shareholders holding eligible voting rights requisition an audit. Private corporations can waive appointment of an auditor through a unanimous shareholder resolution and use a review engagement or unaudited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS, or Canadian ASPE (private-enterprise GAAP) as permitted under the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC register) and update it within 15 business days after any share transfer or other prescribed change. The annual declaration filed with the REQ confirms current directors, officers, and registered office information; any material ISC change must be reflected in the register at the time of filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I rate plus 11.5% Quebec general rate); Quebec's 3% digital advertising services tax may apply separately to qualifying large digital advertising intermediaries.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: combined 12.2% effective rate on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible active business income (9% federal plus 3.2% Quebec rate); additional Quebec deductions for digital innovation/R&D; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) investment tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via approved EFILE software or CRA's e-file portal; Schedule 125 income statement details; Schedule 1 Part I tax calculation; Schedule 9 associated corporation SBD allocation; T106 related-party transaction information return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period of 12 months unless an alternate period is elected)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance of Part I tax is due no later than 2 months after fiscal year-end, extended to 3 months for an eligible CCPC claiming the SBD with taxable capital below CAD 15,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Page 1, Line 1 (Sales, services, and revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross media-buying billings, performance-based affiliate commissions, lead-generation fees, agency service fees, and any advertising arbitrage revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment; treaty-exempt foreign advertising service income is excluded and reconciled in Schedule 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 125 (Income Statement Information) – Advertising, media placement, and affiliate payout expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify verified media inventory purchases, publisher payouts, SSP/DSP platform fees, data costs, and affiliate commissions as deductible operating expenses subject to the reasonableness standard of ITA s. 67.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain non-resident vendor contracts, platform settlement statements, invoice trails, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation evidencing arm's length pricing and actual service performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute federal Part I tax at 15% general rate or 9% SBD rate on eligible active business income after provincial abatement; integrate federal foreign tax credits and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SBD is unavailable to corporations not controlled by Canadian residents; foreign tax credits are limited to foreign-source income and may require the T2 Schedule 21 supporting calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate the CAD 500,000 federal SBD business limit among associated CCPCs; include Canadian affiliates linked through a non-resident parent or common controller.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian corporation more than 50% owned by a non-resident person is associated with sister Canadian corporations under common foreign control; the business limit is divided, not multiplied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months under ITA s. 162(1); repeat offender: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; gross negligence penalty: 50% of understated tax under s. 163(2); daily interest at CRA prescribed rates; separate daily penalties for failure to file T106 information returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 (Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return) filed with Revenu Quebec through the Revenu Quebec e-services filing platform (Cliquez-Déclaration); integrated reconciliation with the federal T2 return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due date is the same as the federal return: 6 months after fiscal year-end; Quebec balance due generally 2 months after fiscal year-end, with the 3-month extension for an eligible CCPC mirroring federal rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile net income from the financial statements with Quebec Taxation Act adjustments, including advertising expense add-backs for overstated media prepayments and accrual adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income earned through a Quebec permanent establishment is taxable; income earned outside Quebec by a non-resident-controlled Canadian corporation is allocated according to the permanent establishment formula.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the Quebec SBD of 3.2% on the qualifying portion of active business income after applying the associated-corporation allocation of the provincial business limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled by non-residents is generally disqualified from the Quebec SBD; only Canadian-controlled qualifying corporations may claim the reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State final taxable income after loss carryforwards, intercorporate dividend deductions, and treaty-based exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-protected business income (no Quebec permanent establishment) is excluded; any withheld Quebec digital advertising services tax should be reviewed with the tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Quebec imposes late filing penalties of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest at prescribed rates; gross negligence penalties of 50% for false statements under the Quebec Taxation Act; additional determinations may be imposed for failure to respond to demand.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under ITA s. 212(2) on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to any non-resident shareholder; no deduction is allowed to the Canadian payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a completed NR301 declaration of residency (or NR302 for exemption claims) and, where required, an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority to the Canadian withholding agent before payment; the payer withholds at the applicable treaty rate after reasonable due diligence, reports withheld amounts on NR4 information returns, and remits Part XIII tax to the CRA. Typical treaty rates for dividends: 5% for a beneficial owner holding 10% or more (Canada-US and Canada-China DTA, generally), otherwise 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding: 25% under ITA s. 212(1)(d); statutory interest withholding: 25% under s. 212(1)(b) subject to exemptions for certain arm's length interest. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10% (with 0% in some treaty contexts for cultural copyrights) and interest to 10% to 15% for related parties, with 0% arm's length interest under the Canada-US treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 filing required when transactions with any one non-resident non-arm's length person exceed CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate FMV; Schedule 10 Local File is triggered when gross revenue is at least CAD 20,000,000 and specified related-party transaction values exceed CAD 5,000,000; Schedule 25 Master File and Schedule 91 Country-by-Country Report apply to MNE groups with consolidated revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000,000; contemporaneous documentation is nonetheless administratively required under ITA s. 247(4) for all material related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone decree-based ESR regime applies in Canada or Quebec; however, economic substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s. 245 and Quebec Taxation Act s. 1079.2), the sham doctrine, and treaty limitation-on-benefits provisions. A Quebec affiliate media-buying vehicle must maintain real employees, office premises, contractual control over media planning and risk exposure, and substantive decision-making; otherwise the CRA or Revenu Quebec may disregard the intermediary, recharacterize transactions, or deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Fictitious Advertising and Lead-Gen Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax deductions for fabricated media placement invoices, circular self-billing between shell traffic brokers, inflated lead prices, or payments for services never actually delivered; deliberately omitting taxable revenue from performance media arbitrage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 14 years; civil reassessment with gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under s. 163(2); prescribed interest compounded daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed, signed, or acquiesced in false filings are jointly and severally liable for withholdings and penalties under s. 227.1; individual criminal exposure includes fines, imprisonment, restitution orders, seizure of assets, and potential travel restrictions while criminal proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Intermediary Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Quebec affiliate media-buying corporation with no real staff, no Canadian office, no risk-bearing budget, and circular routing of advertising spend through a non-resident related party solely to erode Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the arm's length standard of ITA s. 247(2), transfer pricing adjustment penalty of 10% of the net adjustment when documentation is absent or unreliable under s. 247(3), secondary adjustments deemed as shareholder benefit or dividend, denial of deductions, and application of GAAR with a 25% penalty on tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors can be assessed for penalties connected with wilful participation in sham arrangements; personal civil liability may include restitution of corporate tax liabilities where the corporation is stripped or insolvent, and criminal charges under s. 239 for participating in the false arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Unregistered Money Services Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-velocity ACH, wire, or Wise payment volumes for foreign advertisers and publishers without maintaining FINTRAC compliance programs, customer due diligence, or suspicious transaction reporting; using the media-buying entity as an unregistered money services business to launder proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) up to CAD 500,000 per violation for entities; Criminal Code s. 462.31 laundering offense punishable by imprisonment up to 10 years; asset restraint and forfeiture orders; additional state penalties in Quebec under the Act respecting the prevention of money-laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate unregistered money movement face criminal liability, imprisonment, personal fines, FINTRAC compliance orders, asset freezes, travel bans under bail conditions, and exclusion from serving as officers of any federally regulated corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Part XIII Withholdings and Deficient T106 Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising cross-border dividends as management fees, media commissions, or royalties paid to a non-resident parent without withholding 25% Part XIII tax; failing to file T106 related-party transaction returns and NR4 withholding summaries; using artificial prepayment arrangements to shift profits offshore without contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full Part XIII withholding tax against the Canadian payer under ITA s. 215, plus penalties under s. 227(8) of 10% of the unreported amount where failure is willful, daily compounding interest, late-filing penalties for information returns under s. 162(7), and transfer pricing penalties where intercompany charges are non-arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under s. 227.1 for the corporation's unremitted Part XIII withholdings even after corporate dissolution; criminal prosecution under s. 239 can result in imprisonment up to 14 years, personal restitution orders, civil fraud awards, and travel bans imposed by the court.
